widget_margin.description: The Outer Margin of Widgets on the Home Page

quick_settings_height.description: How much of the screen height the quick settings panel takes. A share rather than a pixel count, so one value suits any display. A third is tight on 1080; 0.45 gives the System side room without scrolling. Clamped to 0.15-0.9.

pinned.description: The Path to your Pinned Image for the Home Background

images.description: Home Background's Path for Cycling Images

background_cycle_interval.description: The amount of time in seconds before the background cycles to a new Wallpaper

background_fade_duration.description: How long the fade animation should be when a Wallpaper cycles

output_device.description: Where the panel plays sound. 'Default' follows whatever the system is using, which changes when a USB device is plugged in - a microphone array with a speaker jack will take the output as well as the input unless it is named here.

input_device.description: Which microphone the assistant listens with. 'Default' follows the system.

mic_processing.description: What the microphone does for itself. 'software' assumes a plain mic and cleans the audio here. 'hardware' is for arrays that already do it - the ReSpeaker XVF3800 and similar - and turns off the second pass, because cleaning already-clean audio is what makes speech sound underwater. Set this to hardware only if the device really does the work; on a plain mic it will hear far less.

tts_enabled.description: Whether the assistant speaks its replies. Uses Kyutai Pocket TTS, which runs locally on the CPU and needs no key. A skill that would have spoken shows its answer instead when this is off.

tts_backend.description: Whether to speak replies. 'auto' and 'pocket' both use Kyutai Pocket TTS - local, no key, CPU only. 'off' silences them.

tts_voice.description: Pocket TTS voice. 21 English, plus estelle (fr), giovanni (it), juergen (de), lola (es), rafael (pt). Overridden by Tts Voice File when that is set.

tts_language.description: Pocket TTS language weights. 'default' uses the model's own.

tts_voice_file.description: A wav to clone instead of a listed voice - a local path or an hf:// URL. Overrides Tts Voice. The sample's audio quality is reproduced, so a clean recording matters more than a long one.

tts_padding_ms.description: Silence added either side of a spoken reply. The model stops when the sentence stops, so a one-line answer otherwise begins and ends hard. Also covers the moment a Bluetooth speaker takes to wake, which eats the first syllable. Pocket TTS only.

tts_rate.description: Playback speed. Pocket TTS has no rate control, so this changes the sample rate instead - which moves the PITCH with the speed. 0.95 is audibly less hurried and hard to notice; below about 0.9 it sounds like a slowed recording. Pocket TTS only.

do_not_disturb.description: Hold back notifications and every sound the panel makes. They are still written to the notification history - the point is not to be interrupted, not to lose what happened.

mute_sounds.description: Silence the panel's own sounds and its spoken replies, while leaving notifications on screen. Do not disturb implies this; this does not imply do not disturb.

notification_duration.description: How long a notification stays on screen

notification_queue_delay.description: The delay in seconds between notifications in queue

username.description: Your Username for your music API

panel_name.description: What to call this panel. Shown in Info and on the web pages this panel serves. Empty means the application name.

size.description: Set the size of the window. NOTE: this doesn't effect the actual size, its a reference

position.description: Where the window will position itself on startup

auto_lock.description: Whether the app will automatically on startup, position at X and Y, then fullscreen

interaction_timeout.description: Time of inactivity (no clicks/touches anywhere) before Client fires on_interaction_timeout. Used in the settings page to go home when no interaction has happened for a while.

check_interval.description: How often to ask GitHub whether a newer version exists. This is a single small request, not a download - nothing is fetched until you choose to update. Set to 0 to never check automatically.

restart_on_crash.description: Whether the launcher automatically restarts the app if it crashes. Turn this off to have a crash simply stop the app.

max_restart_attempts.description: How many times in a row the launcher will restart after a crash before giving up. Prevents a boot loop when something is genuinely broken.

crash_window.description: If the app ran longer than this before crashing, the restart counter resets. A long-lived session that later dies is not a boot loop.

update_grace_period.description: If a freshly-applied update crashes within this window, the launcher rolls back to the previous version and relaunches it.

mode.description: How to dim the screen. 'auto' tries real backlight control and falls back to the overlay. 'overlay' never touches the hardware. Or name one: sysfs, logind, ddcutil, brightnessctl, light.

device.description: Which display, if the machine has more than one. A name from /sys/class/backlight, or a ddcutil display number. Blank picks the first that works.

floor.description: Below this the dark overlay takes over, for monitors whose own minimum is still too bright. 0 lets the hardware cover the whole range.

enabled.description: Whether the voice assistant runs at all. Turn this off to stop the speech-to-text process entirely.

model.description:
What transcribes the phrase you said.

parakeet-v3 is NVIDIA's, run through onnx-asr. It covers 25 European languages, and unlike whisper it does not invent words out of silence - which is why nothing here has to filter its output. parakeet-v2 is English-only and slightly faster.

The weights download once on first use, after you are asked. See 'parakeet_precision' for how large that is.

parakeet_precision.description:
Which Parakeet weights to use. Ignored on the whisper models.

'int8' is 700MB, loads faster and runs faster on a panel with no GPU. 'float32' is the full-size export - 2.5GB to download and several times the memory - and is more accurate on long audio, which a phrase said to a wall panel is not. Change this and the new weights download the next time the assistant starts.

wake_word.description:
The word that wakes the assistant, spotted by openWakeWord - a model trained for the job rather than a transcription that gets read.

The list is the words openWakeWord ships models for. Anything else would need a model trained for it, which is a real piece of work and not something the panel can do.

Plugins use this as the default wake word for their skills. The assistant restarts itself when this changes.

wake_listen_timeout.description: How long the panel keeps listening after the wake word before giving up. Too short and it stops mid-thought; too long and it sits listening to the room.

session_silence.description: How long a pause ends your sentence once the assistant is in a conversation. Lower reacts faster; too low and a breath mid-sentence is treated as the end, which splits one question into several and sends each of them separately. 800ms suits normal speech.

wake_sensitivity.description:
How sure openWakeWord has to be before it counts as the wake word.

0.5 is the library's own suggestion. LOWER hears the word through more noise - a fan, music, a room away - and also fires on more things that were not it. HIGHER wants a clearer say of it and misses more.

Worth moving in steps of 0.05 and living with for a day: the cost of going too low is the panel waking up on its own, which is more annoying than saying the word twice. The assistant restarts itself when this changes.

wake_sensitivity_speaking.description:
The same bar, for the moment the panel is talking. 0 means use the ordinary sensitivity above.

While a reply is being read out the microphone carries the panel's own voice alongside yours, so the wake word arrives buried in a way it never is in a quiet room - and the setting that works for the room is often too high for this.

Going lower costs less here than it does elsewhere: a false fire only interrupts a sentence the panel was already reading out. Try 0.05 below the ordinary one and keep going while it still refuses to be interrupted. The assistant restarts itself when this changes.

voice_bar.description: Show the thin activity bar along the bottom of the screen while the assistant is listening.

voice_bar_hold.description: Minimum time the activity bar keeps a transcript on screen. Longer transcripts are held longer than this automatically.

greet_on_start.description: Whether the assistant says hello out loud when it starts listening. The notification appears either way; this is only whether it is spoken. Off by default - a panel that restarts itself at four in the morning should not announce it.

enabled.description: Developer controls and extra logging. Plugins may add their own switches while this is on.
